selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and fresh-squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Overnight Desert Camp in the Sahara
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga as the sun sets, then spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a sky full of stars. Enjoy a campfire dinner with tagine and mint tea, traditional music, and wake up to a breathtaking desert sunrise.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina and Historic Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a knowledgeable local guide. Visit the Medersa Ben Youssef, the historic Koutoubia Mosque, and the vibrant souks selling spices, leather goods, and handwoven carpets. Learn about centuries of Moroccan craftsmanship and Islamic architecture.

experiences.name: Visit the Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's royal past with a self-guided or lightly guided visit to two of Marrakech's most stunning historic sites. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with intricate zellij tilework and carved cedar ceilings, while the 16th-century Saadian Tombs offer a hauntingly beautiful glimpse into dynastic history.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Erg Chebbi Dunes
experiences.description: Get your adrenaline pumping by sandboarding down the towering rust-red dunes of Erg Chebbi. Local operators provide boards and brief instruction, making it accessible for beginners and thrilling for experienced adventurers. Combine with quad biking for an extra desert adventure at minimal additional cost.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take a petit taxi or pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in Marrakech (negotiate fare before boarding — budget around 70–100 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack from a 24-hour convenience store or hotel reception upon arrival — keep it light tonight

day_by_day.notes: Petit taxis are the cheapest airport transfer option. Agree on the fare before getting in. Have small Moroccan dirhams ready if possible. Exchange money at the airport or use an ATM upon arrival. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, head to the legendary Djemaa el-Fna square for a classic Marrakech morning. Explore the bustling square and wander into the nearby souks (Souk Semmarine, Souk el-Attarine). Haggle for spices, leather goods, and handmade crafts. Visit the free-entry exterior of the Koutoubia Mosque and its beautiful gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) — a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis. Afterward, explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) for sweeping rooftop views and rich history. Walk through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and admire the ornate architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at sunset when the square transforms into a massive open-air spectacle — snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and food stalls everywhere. Soak in the atmosphere and enjoy the vibrant energy of Marrakech by night.

meals.breakfast: Café des Épices or a local café near the medina — mint tea, msemen (Moroccan flatbread), and amlou (almond-argan dip) for under 30 MAD
meals.lunch: Street food at the souks — harira soup, kefta sandwich, or a bowl of snail soup from a market stall (20–40 MAD total)
meals.dinner: Eat at the Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — choose stall No. 1 or 14 for grilled meats, couscous, and Moroccan salads. Full meal for 50–80 MAD. Avoid tourist traps by checking prices on the menu board first.

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected in the souks — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a close eye on your belongings in crowded areas. Dress modestly out of respect for local culture (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring its 160 rooms and lush courtyards. Afterward, stroll through the Mellah market for fresh produce and local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum area (Majorelle Garden entry ~100 MAD — worth the splurge for the iconic blue villa and exotic plant collection). If budget is tight, admire the exterior walls and surrounding neighborhood. Visit the nearby Gueliz district (the New City) for a change of pace — modern cafés, galleries, and tree-lined boulevards.
day_by_day.evening: Take a calèche (horse-drawn carriage) ride around the ramparts of the medina at sunset — a classic Marrakech experience. Negotiate a price (around 150–200 MAD for the carriage, split among your group). End the evening with a hammam experience at a local public hammam like Hammam Bab Doukkala (entry ~15–20 MAD for locals' rate).

meals.breakfast: Café Clock Marrakech — avocado toast or Moroccan breakfast platter, budget-friendly with great ambiance (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Chez Lamine Hadj Mustapha near Djemaa el-Fna — famous for mechoui (slow-roasted lamb). Half portion with bread ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad Yima rooftop café or a local Moroccan restaurant in the medina — tagine with bread and mint tea for ~60–90 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Majorelle Garden can get crowded mid-morning — arrive right when it opens at 8:00 AM for a more peaceful experience. The public hammam is a genuine cultural experience — bring flip-flops and a towel.

day_by_day.morning: Early start! Depart Marrakech by 7:00–8:00 AM on a shared budget tour or CTM bus toward the Sahara Desert via the Dades Valley route (book a 2-day shared desert tour in advance — budget options start from 350–500 MAD per person including transport and basic accommodation). Pass through the stunning Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude) in the High Atlas Mountains with breathtaking panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and ancient ksar (fortified village) famously used as a filming location for Game of Thrones and Gladiator. Explore the mud-brick citadel on foot (small entry donation ~10–20 MAD). Cross the river on stepping stones for the full experience. Continue driving through the dramatic Draa Valley and Dadès Gorge landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the Merzouga/Erg Chebbi area at the edge of the Sahara by late evening. Check into a budget desert camp or basic auberge (included in tour package or ~150–200 MAD standalone). Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner around a campfire under the stars — a magical experience in the silence of the desert.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a café near the departure point in Marrakech — coffee, bread, and jam (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside restaurant near Aït Benhaddou — tagine and Berber bread (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — harira soup, tagine, couscous, and Moroccan mint tea (usually included in tour package)

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared desert tour at least 1–2 days in advance from a reputable agency in Marrakech (check reviews on TripAdvisor or Hostelworld). The drive is long (~8–9 hours total with stops) but the scenery is spectacular. Bring a warm layer — desert nights can be cold in March.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 5:30–6:00 AM) for a camel trek into the Erg Chebbi sand dunes — one of the most iconic experiences in Morocco. Ride to the top of a dune and watch the sunrise paint the Sahara in shades of orange and gold. Spend time sandboarding (boards often available at camp for a small fee ~20–30 MAD) and photographing the endless sea of dunes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for breakfast, then explore the nearby village of Merzouga on foot or by bicycle (rentals ~30–50 MAD/hour). Visit a local Gnawa musician's home for an impromptu performance, or explore a fossil and mineral shop (no obligation to buy). Head to the Dayet Srji salt lake (seasonal) on the outskirts of Merzouga — flamingos sometimes gather here in spring.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech (if on a 2-day tour) or spend a second night in the desert. If returning, travel via the scenic Ziz Valley and Erfoud. Alternatively, stop overnight in Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — and visit the famous Atlas Film Studios (entry ~60 MAD), one of the largest film studios in the world.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the desert camp after the sunrise camel trek — Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, eggs, and mint tea (included in most packages)
meals.lunch: Local café in Merzouga village — Berber omelette, fresh bread, and tea (~30–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Ouarzazate if stopping overnight — chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives (~60–80 MAD) at a local spot like Restaurant Es Salam

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf for the dunes — the sun is strong even in March. Tip your camel guide (20–30 MAD is appreciated). If staying a second night in the desert, negotiate directly with your camp for a discount.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Marrakech via shared transport or bus (depart early to maximize your last full day). If time permits, stop at the Roses Valley near Kelaat M'Gouna — in mid-March the rose bushes are beginning to bloom ahead of the famous Rose Festival. Explore small Berber villages along the Dadès Gorge with dramatic rock formations and cliff-side kasbahs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early-to-mid afternoon. Visit the Museum of Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century palace — excellent Moroccan art and artifact collections. Stop at the nearby Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD) — a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellij tilework, carved stucco, and a serene central courtyard.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the medina — revisit your favorite spots in the souks for any last-minute souvenir shopping. Head to a rooftop café overlooking Djemaa el-Fna for sunset drinks (fresh-squeezed orange juice ~5 MAD from the square itself). Enjoy a relaxed final dinner in the medina.

meals.breakfast: On the road — stop at a roadside café or argan oil cooperative for mint tea and msemen (~15–25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a local snack shop in the medina upon return — merguez sandwich or kefta wrap (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — try Le Jardin restaurant in the medina for a beautiful courtyard setting and Moroccan cuisine (~100–150 MAD per person, still budget-friendly by Western standards)

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa and Museum of Marrakech combo ticket saves money. If you're exhausted from the desert trip, feel free to swap the museum visits for a relaxing hammam session and souk stroll instead.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final morning in Marrakech. Take one last walk through the medina at dawn when it's quietest and most atmospheric — the golden morning light on the ancient walls is unforgettable. Visit the Cyber Park Arset Moulay Abdeslam (free entry) — a peaceful green space perfect for a quiet morning stroll. Pick up any final souvenirs: argan oil, saffron, Moroccan leather slippers (babouches), or handmade ceramics from the souks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, check out of the hotel and head to the airport. Marrakech Menara Airport is only 6 km from the city center — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Take a petit taxi (70–100 MAD) or the airport bus (Line 19, ~10–15 MAD) to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Carry wonderful memories of Morocco's colors, flavors, and desert landscapes!

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a medina café — mint tea, msemen, honey, and amlou (~25–35 MAD). A perfect farewell to Morocco!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick bite near the hotel before checkout — harira soup and bread (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep some dirhams for your taxi to the airport and any last-minute purchases. Note that Moroccan dirhams cannot be exported in large quantities — spend remaining cash or exchange back at the airport. Leave a review for your riad/hotel and tour guides to help future budget travelers!

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. If the hotel kitchen is still open, grab a light late-night snack at the hotel bar or lounge.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack at the hotel upon arrival — try Moroccan mint tea and a small mezze plate if available at the hotel lounge

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival, keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Confirm your itinerary details with the hotel concierge the next morning. Pre-arrange your airport transfer in advance to avoid delays at night.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. After breakfast, head into the heart of Marrakech's UNESCO-listed Medina. Begin with a visit to the stunning Koutoubia Mosque (exterior view) and stroll through Jemaa el-Fna Square, soaking in the vibrant atmosphere of street performers, orange juice vendors, and snake charmers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework and lush gardens. Afterward, wander through the colorful souks of the Medina — browse leather goods, spices, lanterns, and textiles. Visit the famous Dyers' Souk (Souk Sabbaghin) for a burst of color.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna Square at sunset when it truly comes alive with food stalls, musicians, and storytellers. Dine at one of the square's rooftop restaurants for panoramic views over the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Moroccan staples like msemen (flatbread), honey, argan oil, and fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local Medina café — try a chicken tagine or harira soup with bread (~60–100 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café de France rooftop or Le Marrakchi restaurant near Jemaa el-Fna — enjoy pastilla (pigeon pie) or lamb couscous (~150–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes as the Medina streets are cobblestoned and uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep small change handy for tips.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a hidden 16th-century royal necropolis with beautifully preserved mausoleums. Then explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace offering great views from its ramparts. History lovers will be captivated by the scale and story of both sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to discover Marrakech's multicultural heritage, including the historic Lazama Synagogue. Visit the nearby Maison de la Photographie for a fascinating collection of vintage Moroccan photographs (~50 MAD entry). Spend the late afternoon at the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (entry ~150 MAD) — a stunning blue garden oasis designed by Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Moroccan hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or Bain Marrakchi (~200–350 MAD for a full scrub and massage). Afterward, dine in the Gueliz (New City) neighborhood for a more relaxed, modern atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riad restaurant in the Mellah area — try a Moroccan salad spread with kefta skewers (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Grand Café de la Poste in Gueliz — a colonial-era brasserie serving Moroccan-French fusion cuisine (~150–220 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden online in advance — it sells out quickly. The hammam is best experienced in the late afternoon/early evening. March weather in Marrakech is mild (~18–24°C), perfect for outdoor exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–8:00 AM) by private or shared transfer toward the Sahara Desert via the scenic Draa Valley route. Stop at the stunning Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas Mountains for breathtaking panoramic views and photos. Continue to Ouarzazate, the 'Gateway to the Sahara,' and visit the impressive Aït Benhaddou Ksar (UNESCO World Heritage Site, ~30 MAD entry) — a fortified mud-brick city used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through the Valley of Roses (Kalaat M'Gouna) and the dramatic Todra Gorge or Draa Valley landscapes. Arrive at your desert camp accommodation near Merzouga or Zagora by late afternoon. Check in to a mid-range desert camp with private tents and en-suite facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a magical 45-minute trek into the Erg Chebbi sand dunes. Watch the sunset paint the dunes in shades of gold and orange from a high dune vantage point. Return to camp for a traditional Berber dinner under a canopy of stars, accompanied by live Gnawa drumming and music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure or packed breakfast from the hotel
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch in Ouarzazate at a local restaurant near Aït Benhaddou — try a lamb tagine with prunes (~80–130 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — Moroccan couscous, tagine, Berber bread, and mint tea (~included in camp package or ~150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~8–10 hours driving). Hiring a private driver is recommended for comfort (~600–900 MAD per person for a shared tour or ~2,500–3,500 MAD for a private vehicle). Book your desert camp well in advance. Bring a light jacket — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (~6:00 AM) and climb the nearest sand dune to watch the spectacular Sahara sunrise — one of the most memorable experiences of the trip. After breakfast at camp, explore the Erg Chebbi dunes on foot or by quad bike (optional adventure activity, ~200–300 MAD for 1 hour). Visit a nearby Berber nomad family for an authentic cultural exchange and tea ceremony.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the small town of Merzouga for a walk through its local market and the Gnawa musicians' quarter. Explore the Dayet Srji salt lake (seasonal — may have flamingos in spring). Begin the journey back toward Marrakech, stopping at the Todra Gorge (if not visited on Day 4) — a dramatic canyon with 300m-high rose-colored rock walls, ideal for a short scenic hike.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight in a mid-range riad or hotel in Boumalne Dades or Ouarzazate to break up the return journey. Enjoy a quiet dinner and rest after the adventurous desert experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the desert camp — Berber pancakes (msemen), honey, argan oil, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch in Merzouga town at a local café — try a mixed Moroccan salad and grilled kefta (~70–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your overnight stop riad or a local restaurant — lamb tagine with vegetables (~100–150 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise over the Sahara is unmissable — set multiple alarms. Wear sunscreen and a hat for daytime dune activities. If quad biking, ensure helmets are provided. The return drive from Merzouga to Marrakech is approximately 9–10 hours total, so breaking it into two days is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Continue the scenic drive back to Marrakech through the Draa Valley and High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the charming Skoura Oasis for a short walk through its ancient palm grove and historic kasbahs, including Kasbah Amridil (~20 MAD entry). Enjoy the contrast between the lush oasis and the arid desert landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early-to-mid afternoon. Freshen up at the hotel. Spend the afternoon at leisure — revisit any missed souks, pick up last-minute souvenirs, or relax at the hotel pool. Alternatively, take a short excursion to the Menara Gardens and Agdal Gardens for a peaceful stroll among olive groves and reflecting pools.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell Marrakech evening with a special dinner at a traditional Moroccan riad restaurant. Splurge slightly on a memorable meal in a beautiful courtyard setting. After dinner, take one last stroll through Jemaa el-Fna Square to soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your overnight riad/hotel in Boumalne Dades or Ouarzazate
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a quick stop at a roadside café en route — Moroccan sandwiches (kefta in khobz bread) and fresh juice (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a Marrakech riad restaurant such as Dar Yacout, Nomad, or Le Foundouk — try bastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb mechoui, and Moroccan pastries for dessert (~200–350 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the riad dinner restaurant in advance, especially for weekend evenings. The drive back from the desert is long but scenic — bring music, podcasts, or a good book. March is an excellent time for the Draa Valley as wildflowers may be in bloom.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Depending on your flight time, take a relaxed morning walk through the quieter early-morning streets of the Medina — the souks are peaceful before 9:00 AM and you can see locals going about their daily routines. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD) if not yet seen — a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate stucco and cedar woodwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout. Allow ample time for the transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport (approximately 15–20 minutes from the Medina, but allow 30–45 minutes for traffic). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for international departures.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Marrakech with unforgettable memories of souks, desert dunes, mountain passes, and Berber culture.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy a full Moroccan spread one last time
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Medina before heading to the airport — try a quick bowl of harira soup with chebakia pastry at a local café (~30–50 MAD) or grab a snack at the airport
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Keep some Moroccan dirhams for last-minute tips, airport snacks, or duty-free shopping. Note that dirhams cannot be exchanged outside Morocco, so spend or exchange remaining currency before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. A private luxury transfer in a Mercedes-Benz S-Class will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a traditional Moroccan welcome with rose water, mint tea, and warm pastries. Check in, freshen up, and unwind in your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – travel day
meals.lunch: Not applicable – travel day
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter arranged by the resort: Moroccan mezze, fresh dates, artisan cheeses, and chilled Moroccan rosé served in your suite

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer pre-arranged. Request a late-night turndown service with aromatherapy oils and a hammam appointment booked for Day 2 morning. Keep luggage unpacking minimal – let the butler service assist.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a restorative Royal Hammam & Argan Oil Massage at the resort's luxury spa (90 minutes). Follow with a leisurely breakfast on your private terrace. At 10:30, embark on a private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Medina – explore the labyrinthine souks of Mellah, the dazzling Bahia Palace, and the ornate Ben Youssef Madrasa with your expert local historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a gourmet lunch, visit the Saadian Tombs – a hidden jewel of 16th-century Moroccan architecture. Continue to the iconic Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a serene stroll. Head to the legendary Jardin Majorelle, the electric-blue garden sanctuary once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, and explore the adjacent Berber Museum. Private transport between all sites.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk to witness the magical transformation – storytellers, musicians, and snake charmers under a canopy of stars. Dine at La Mamounia's Le Français restaurant, one of Morocco's most celebrated fine-dining establishments, featuring contemporary French-Moroccan fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Lavish à la carte breakfast at the resort – fresh Moroccan breads (msemen, harcha), amlou (almond-argan spread), fresh-squeezed orange juice, eggs royale, and Berber herbal tea
meals.lunch: Nomad Marrakech – a rooftop restaurant with panoramic Medina views; signature lamb pastilla, preserved lemon chicken tagine, and house-made lemonade
meals.dinner: La Mamounia – Le Français: 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring Moroccan-inspired French gastronomy in an opulent 1920s Art Deco setting

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina. Dress modestly when entering religious and historic sites (shoulders and knees covered). The private guide will navigate the souks to avoid tourist traps and find authentic artisan workshops.

day_by_day.morning: Depart at 08:00 in a private 4x4 luxury vehicle toward the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the scenic Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m elevation) for breathtaking panoramic photography. Visit the ancient fortified village of Aït Benhaddou – a UNESCO World Heritage ksar that has starred in Game of Thrones and Gladiator – with your private historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a traditional Berber village in the Ourika Valley for an authentic home-hosted lunch experience. Participate in a private cooking class learning to prepare a classic Moroccan tagine and hand-rolled couscous with a local Berber family. Explore terraced saffron and herb gardens. Return journey via the scenic Ourika Valley with a stop at a local argan oil cooperative run by Berber women.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by 18:30. Enjoy sunset cocktails at the resort's rooftop terrace. Dine at Dar Yacout – a legendary riad restaurant set in a 17th-century palace with candlelit courtyards, live Gnawa music, and an extraordinary 7-course Moroccan feast.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort – Moroccan pastries, fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee before 08:00 departure
meals.lunch: Immersive Berber home-hosted lunch in the Atlas Mountains: slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, fresh-baked bread, Moroccan salads, and mint tea
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout: 7-course traditional Moroccan banquet – harira soup, bastilla, multiple tagines, couscous royale, and honey-drenched pastries with live traditional music

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light jacket – Atlas Mountain temperatures can drop significantly even in March. The cooking class is hands-on; wear casual clothing. Aït Benhaddou visit is best in morning light for photography. Confirm Dar Yacout reservation 48 hours in advance as it books quickly.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 – March 18, 2027 (Journey to the Sahara – Day 1 of 2)
day_by_day.morning: Check out from the resort after a leisurely breakfast. At 08:00, depart in a private luxury 4x4 convoy toward the Draa Valley and Sahara Desert. En route, stop at the spectacular Draa Valley – Morocco's longest river valley – lined with thousands of date palms and ancient kasbahs. Visit the Tamnougalt Kasbah, a 16th-century fortified palace, for a private tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south through dramatic lunar landscapes and vast hammada (rocky desert plateaus). Stop at Erg Chebbi's gateway town of Merzouga for a traditional lunch. At 15:30, transition from vehicles to private luxury camel caravan for a 90-minute golden-hour trek into the dunes of Erg Chebbi – Morocco's most spectacular sand sea, with dunes rising up to 150 meters.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your exclusive private luxury desert camp – a collection of bespoke Berber tents with en-suite bathrooms, plush bedding, solar lighting, and private outdoor seating. Witness a spectacular Saharan sunset from the top of a private dune with chilled Champagne. After dark, enjoy a private stargazing session with a telescope guided by an astronomy expert. Dine under a billion stars with live Gnawa drumming around a fire.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort – full Moroccan spread with fresh-pressed juices, pastries, eggs, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Kasbah Panorama Restaurant, Merzouga – traditional Moroccan tagine, Mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), fresh salads, and fresh-squeezed cactus juice
meals.dinner: Private camp gourmet dinner under the stars: Moroccan mezze, slow-cooked camel tagine, Berber couscous, fresh flatbreads, and traditional sweets with Saharan herbal tea and fine Moroccan wines

day_by_day.notes: Pack a small overnight bag for the camel trek – main luggage will be transported by 4x4 to the camp. Temperatures drop sharply in the desert at night (can reach 5–10°C in March); the camp provides premium wool blankets and fleece-lined djellabas. Bring a headlamp, lip balm, and sunscreen. Phone signal is minimal – embrace the digital detox.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private sunrise hike to the summit of the highest nearby dune – a truly transcendent experience as golden light floods the Sahara. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast in the open desert. At 09:00, choose your adventure: private sandboarding on the mega-dunes, a quad biking excursion across the erg, or a meditative solo dune walk with your guide. Visit a nomadic Tuareg family encampment for authentic tea ceremony and cultural exchange.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart camp by camel at 11:00, returning to Merzouga. Board your private 4x4 for the return journey north, stopping at the stunning Todra Gorge – a dramatic 300-meter-high canyon carved by the Todra River – for a private guided walk through the narrow canyon floor. Lunch at a cliffside restaurant overlooking the gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Continue to the charming town of Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Morocco' – and check into a luxury kasbah hotel for one night. Explore the illuminated Taourirt Kasbah at dusk. Dinner at a private rooftop restaurant with views of the Atlas Mountains.

meals.breakfast: Saharan camp breakfast: fresh Berber flatbreads baked in sand, honey, olive oil, Amlou spread, hard-boiled eggs, fresh dates, and mint tea at sunrise
meals.lunch: Restaurant Les Roches, Todra Gorge – grilled kefta, Berber pizza (medfouna), fresh salads, and freshly squeezed orange juice with canyon views
meals.dinner: Dar Kamar, Ouarzazate – intimate riad restaurant; rooftop dining featuring slow-roasted lamb mechoui, vegetable couscous, and Moroccan dessert platter with rose water ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Sandboarding and quad biking are included in the luxury camp package. The Todra Gorge walk is easy to moderate – suitable for all fitness levels. Ouarzazate is approximately 3 hours from Merzouga. Confirm the luxury kasbah hotel in Ouarzazate is pre-booked before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a private guided tour of the Atlas Film Studios – the world's largest film studios, where Lawrence of Arabia, Gladiator, and countless other epics were filmed. Explore authentic set pieces and costume archives with a film historian. Visit the Kasbah Taourirt in full morning light – one of the finest kasbahs in Morocco, built by the powerful Glaoui dynasty. Browse the adjacent artisan cooperative for premium handwoven carpets, silver jewelry, and leather goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Ouarzazate at 13:00 for the scenic 3.5-hour private drive back to Marrakech via the spectacular Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass. Stop at a high-altitude panoramic viewpoint for photography and a private Berber tea service. Arrive in Marrakech by 17:00. Check back into Aegean Bliss Resort and enjoy a revitalizing resort spa treatment – choose from a traditional Moroccan rhassoul clay body wrap or a Hammam ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening exploring the upscale Gueliz district (New Marrakech) – visit the Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech (YSL Museum) for its stunning permanent collection and Moroccan-inspired fashion exhibitions. Dine at Comptoir Darna – Marrakech's most glamorous supper club, featuring belly dancing performances, live jazz, and exquisite Moroccan-French cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Luxury kasbah hotel breakfast in Ouarzazate – fresh Moroccan pastries, local honey, argan oil, fresh fruit platters, and Berber coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route – private gourmet picnic prepared by the kasbah: artisan sandwiches, Moroccan salads, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling water with mountain views
meals.dinner: Comptoir Darna, Marrakech: 4-course à la carte dinner – signature duck pastilla, lamb shank tagine with preserved lemon, saffron crème brûlée, and curated Moroccan wine selection with live entertainment

day_by_day.notes: The YSL Museum closes on Tuesdays – verify the day before. Comptoir Darna is a vibrant, lively venue; smart-casual dress code applies. The resort spa treatments should be booked in advance. The mountain pass road is winding – take motion sickness precautions if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning at the resort. Indulge in a premium breakfast on your private terrace. At 10:00, embark on a curated luxury shopping experience in the Medina with a personal shopping guide who knows the finest artisan workshops – source hand-knotted Berber carpets, bespoke leather goods from the historic Chouara Tannery, silver Tuareg jewelry, hand-painted zellige tiles, and premium argan-based beauty products. Visit the hidden atelier of a master Moroccan craftsman for a private demonstration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final poolside lunch. Spend the early afternoon at leisure – enjoy the resort's infinity pool, beachfront cabana, or indulge in one final spa treatment. At 15:00, begin packing and prepare for departure. A private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport departs at 17:00 (adjust timing based on your departure flight).
day_by_day.evening: Airport transfer and departure. If the flight is late evening, enjoy a final Moroccan mint tea and pastry at the airport's VIP lounge.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort – the full Moroccan luxury spread: msemen pancakes with honey and butter, shakshuka, fresh-squeezed juice, artisan pastries, and specialty Berber coffee
meals.lunch: Final poolside lunch at the resort – Moroccan-inspired mezze platter, grilled sea bass chermoula, saffron rice, and a chilled glass of Moroccan Gris rosé
meals.dinner: Airport VIP lounge or light in-flight dining – request the resort to prepare a gourmet departure hamper with Moroccan sweets, dates, and artisan snacks for the journey

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for shopping – the Medina can be time-consuming. Ship larger carpet or tile purchases directly from the artisan workshop to avoid excess baggage fees (most premium workshops offer international shipping). Keep receipts for customs declarations. Tip your private guide and driver generously – 10–15% is customary for luxury service providers in Morocco.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026
